# Adjudication Task — Chapter 276

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃276화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|중년인은 어디에서나 볼 수 있는 흔한 동네 아저씨였다.
  6|
  7|귀밑부터 턱까지 이어진 푸르스름한 수염 자국. 실용성을 강조한 등산복은 뱃살로 불룩하다.
  8|
  9|이른 새벽, 졸음이 뚝뚝 떨어지는 눈으로 스트레칭을 끝낸 그는 논두렁 길을 천천히 뛰기 시작했다.
 10|
 11|헛둘헛둘, 아저씨 특유의 구성진 소리까지 곁들여 가면서.
 12|
 13|김 집사가 찾았다는 ‘꼬리’가 바로 그였다.
 14|
 15|“이 아저씨 맞아요?”
 16|
 17|어디서나 볼 수 있는 승합차 내부, 김 집사가 마법으로 녹화한 영상을 보던 송송이가 미심쩍다는 표정으로 중얼거렸다.
 18|
 19|“평범해 보이는데.”
 20|
 21|“비범해 보이는 게 더 이상하지 않을까. 블랙 헌터가 9급 공무원 같은 느낌은 아니잖아.”
 22|
 23|“아무리 그래도 저 아저씨는 너무 평범해 보여서. 전투 헌터들만 알아볼 수 있는 뭐 그런 게 있나?”
 24|
 25|“있지.”
 26|
 27|나는 조깅을 끝마치고 저택으로 들어가는 중년인의 모습을 뚫어질 듯이 응시했다.
 28|
 29|지금 보는 것은 단순한 영상에 불과하니 공력은 느낄 수 없다. 그러나 아무리 천재적인 연기자라 해도 미세한 움직임 하나에서 자신을 드러내기 마련이다.
 30|
 31|그리고 내게는 연기를 꿰뚫어 볼 수 있는 안목이 있었다.
 32|
 33|“절정 고수…….”
 34|
 35|“응?”
 36|
 37|내 혼잣말에 반응한 사람은 송송이뿐만이 아니었다.
 38|
 39|그게 무슨 소리냐는 듯한 최 팀장과 김 집사의 시선에 말을 이었다.
 40|
 41|“……가 아니라, A급 헌터네요.”
 42|
 43|“뭐라 말씀하셨던 것 같은데. 절정 고수라고 하셨나.”
 44|
 45|“놉. 잘못 들으신 듯.”
 46|
 47|이럴 땐 철벽이 답이다. 당사자가 안 했다는데 어쩔 거야.
 48|
 49|석연찮은 눈빛도 잠시, 최 팀장과 김 집사도 내 의견에 동조하듯 고개를 끄덕였다.
 50|
 51|“A급 헌터라는 것에는 저도 같은 의견입니다.”
 52|
 53|“지켜본 바로는 A급 중에서도 제법 상위에 속하는 실력자더군요. 감시 마법을 알아차릴 것 같아 거리를 둘 수밖에 없었습니다.”
 54|
 55|김 집사는 대격변을 치른 역전의 용사인 데다 직접 지켜봤으니 그러려니 하겠는데, 최 팀장은 생각했던 것 이상으로 훨씬 안목이 뛰어나다.
 56|
 57|이건 아무나 알아볼 수 있는 수준이 아닌데.
 58|
 59|‘뭐, 어쨌든 지금은 이게 중요한 게 아니지.’
 60|
 61|나는 가장 궁금했던 것부터 물었다.
 62|
 63|“그런데 어떻게 찾으신 겁니까? 수사팀에서 인근 CCTV도 다 회수해 갔다고 들었는데.”
 64|
 65|“다시 찾아왔습니다.”
 66|
 67|아니, 그러니까 그걸 어떻게 했냐고.
 68|
 69|되물어 보기도 전에 최 팀장이 엄지와 검지를 붙여 동그라미를 만들었다.
 70|
 71|“태경 씨가 말씀하셨었죠. 이건 두루두루 잘 먹힌다고.”
 72|
 73|“아…….”
 74|
 75|“만고불변의 진리입니다. 저도 전부터 애용하는 방법이었고요.”
 76|
 77|수사팀의 누군가에게 뇌물을 찔러 줬군.
 78|
 79|최 팀장의 배포를 생각해 봤을 때, 누군지는 몰라도 한몫 단단히 챙겼을 게 분명했다.
 80|
 81|“외압이 있다고 하지 않았어요?”
 82|
 83|“그럴 때는 외압도 버틸 만큼의 돈을 쥐여 주면 됩니다.”
 84|
 85|그거 굉장하네.
 86|
 87|하지만 이어지는 말을 들어 보니 돈에도 한계가 있었던 모양이다.
 88|
 89|“제법 거물급이 나선 것 같습니다. 어지간해서는 술술 불어야 정상인데…… 겁을 먹었는지 아무리 돈을 퍼먹여도 입을 열지 않더군요. CCTV가 최선이었습니다.”
 90|
 91|“거기에 걸린 놈이 저놈?”
 92|
 93|“네. 일루전(Illusion) 마법이 걸린 아티팩트를 썼는지 약간의 차이는 있었지만 확실합니다.”
 94|
 95|이미 어느 정도 예상은 했지만, 수작질을 부리고 있는 놈들은 상당한 권력자들인 모양이었다.
 96|
 97|한 정당의 최고위원의 입에 기름을 칠하고, 인터넷 여론 조작도 자유자재. 심지어 뇌물을 받아먹을 만큼 부패한 경, 검까지 알아서 몸을 사릴 정도다.
 98|
 99|‘대형 길드인 건 확실한 것 같은데.’
100|
101|20위권 안에 드는 대형 길드라면 가능하다. 그들은 길드라는 이름으로 우뚝 선 재벌 기업과 다름없으니까.
102|
103|블랙 헌터라는 불법 사병 집단까지 육성할 정도니 볼 장 다 본 거지 뭐.
104|
105|“그래서 저놈, 뭐 하는 인간입니까?”
106|
107|“귀농의 로망을 이룬 도시인이죠.”
108|
109|김 집사가 부드럽게 한마디를 덧붙이며 태블릿을 내밀었다.
110|
111|“표면상으로는요.”
112|
113|받아 든 태블릿에는 ‘꼬리’의 모든 것이 담겨 있었다.
114|
115|나이는 이제 40대 중반에 십여 년 전쯤 주식으로 상당한 재산을 모았지만, 지병으로 쓰러지기를 여러 차례 반복한 끝에 귀농을 결심했다고 한다.
116|
117|“지병?”
118|
119|“병원 진단서도 있습니다.”
120|
121|A급 헌터가 지병은 무슨.
122|
123|나는 피식 웃으며 병원 진단서를 휙휙 넘겼다.
124|
125|“이거 다 개소리라는 거에 제 왼쪽 손목 겁니다.”
126|
127|최 팀장이 당연하다는 듯 고개를 끄덕였다.
128|
129|“그럼 전 진태경 씨의 오른쪽 손목을 걸겠습니다.”
130|
131|“…….”
132|
133|이거 미친놈 아냐. 내 손목을 왜 걸어.
134|
135|황당한 시선을 슬쩍 무시한 최 팀장이 말을 이었다.
136|
137|“어쨌건 표면상으로는 완벽한 일반인입니다. 처음 정착했을 때부터 사교성도 좋았고, 2주에 한 번씩 마을 잔치를 열어서 외지인 딱지는 예전에 없어졌다는군요.”
138|
139|“인적 드문 산골 마을에 의심하는 사람도 없다?”
140|
141|“돈 많고 성격 좋은 호인이니까요.”
142|
143|“숨어서 뭐 하기에는 안성맞춤이겠네요. 예를 들면 블랙 헌터들을 육성한다든가.”
144|
145|마지막 화면을 유심히 살폈다.
146|
147|그림 같은 2층 단독 주택. 넓은 마당에 비해 집은 상대적으로 작아 보인다.
148|
149|회색 돌담 옆에는 고급 SUV 한 대와 승용차 한 대가 주차되어 있었다.
150|
151|‘저 안에 몇 명이나 있을까.’
152|
153|임꺽정을 습격한 놈들은 총 셋. 굳이 드래곤볼처럼 하나씩 흩어져 있을 이유는 없으니 저 집 안에 있다고 봐야 한다.
154|
155|아, 잠깐. 잠깐만.
156|
157|“아까 그러셨죠. 2주에 한 번씩 마을 잔치를 연다고.”
158|
159|“네. 그때마다 외부에서 음식 재료를 대량으로 주문하는데…… 아!”
160|
161|마을 잔치는 식료품을 조달하기 위한 위장막일 가능성이 컸다.
162|
163|‘이거, 생각보다 머릿수가 꽤 될지도 모르겠는데.’
164|
165|훈련도 할 테니 나머지 인원은 지하실에 박아 놨나?
166|
167|아니면 주위에 울창한 숲속 어딘가?
168|
169|개인적인 바람이지만 지하실에 옹기종기 모여 있었으면 좋겠다. 그래야 편하니까.
170|
171|“섣부르게 다가갔다가는 되레 당할 수도 있습니다. 그러니 오늘은 이쯤에서…….”
172|
173|“네. 이쯤에서 슬슬 시작하죠.”
174|
175|나는 후드를 푹 눌러쓰고 자동차 문을 열었다.
176|
177|“다녀오겠습니다.”
178|
179|“예?”
180|
181|“나머지 세 분은 20분 후에 오세요. 그때쯤이면 슬슬 끝날 것 같으니까.”
182|
183|세 사람의 당황한 시선이 우수수 날아와 꽂혔다.
184|
185|가장 연륜 있는 김 집사가 먼저 입을 열었다.
186|
187|“진태경 헌터님. 파악되지 않는 적만큼 무서운 건 없습니다.”
188|
189|“네. 알고 있어요.”
190|
191|“실력이 뛰어나신 건 알지만…….”
192|
193|김 집사의 진중한 목소리가 이어졌다.
194|
195|“제가 감시한 자와 같은 A급 헌터 수십 명이 기다리고 있을지도 모른다는 말입니다.”
196|
197|“괜찮아요. 아까 걔보다는 차라리 세 얼간이가 더 강해 보이던데.”
198|
199|“……?”
200|
201|“아, 신경 쓰지 마세요. 그냥 아는 지인이 생각나서.”
202|
203|송송이가 기가 찬다는 듯한 목소리로 물었다.
204|
205|“지금 타이밍에 지인 생각이 나?”
206|
207|“아니, 난 항상 네 생각이 나.”
208|
209|“히익.”
210|
211|“조용히 해. 고백해서 혼내 주기 전에.”
212|
213|“꺄악!”
214|
215|후, 존나 멋있어. 이러니까 여자들이 학을 떼지.
216|
217|오늘도 가뿐하게 1승을 챙기고 승합차에서 내리려던 그때였다.
218|
219|“말리고 싶은데, 말릴 수가 없네요.”
220|
221|최 팀장이 무어라 설명하기 힘든 오묘한 표정으로 말을 이었다.
222|
223|“진태경 씨가 하는 미친 짓은 항상 성공했으니까.”
224|
225|“사람 제대로 보셨네. 그럼 내가 말한 그대로 움직여요. 늦어도 한 시간이면 다 끝날 테니까.”
226|
227|“블랙 헌터…… 그놈들은 몬스터가 아니라 인간을 사냥하는 훈련을 받은 놈들입니다. 조심하십시오.”
228|
229|나는 참지 못하고 실소를 흘렸다.
230|
231|“잘됐네요. 그쪽도 나름 내 전문 분야라서.”
232|
233|“……예?”
234|
235|눈이 휘둥그레진 최 팀장을 뒤로하고 밖으로 나갔다.
236|
237|별 무리가 뿌려진 시골의 밤하늘, 시원한 바람을 폐부 깊숙이 들이마시며 쭉 기지개를 켰다.
238|
239|저 멀리 어둠에 잠긴 블랙 헌터들의 본거지를 향해 걸어가는 나는, 헌터 진태경이 아닌 무림인 진태경이 되어 있었다.
240|
241|
242|
243|* * *
244|
245|
246|
247|크르르르.
248|
249|칠흑 같은 어둠 속에서 짐승의 눈이 번쩍였다.
250|
251|철창 너머에서 나를 향해 이빨을 드러내는 두 마리의 도사견을 향해 살기를 쏘아 보냈다.
252|
253|“개 짖는 소리가 들리면, 너희는 보신탕이 된다.”
254|
255|도사견들이 한국어학당에 다니지 않는 이상 말이 통할 리 없다.
256|
257|하지만 살기(殺氣)는 이야기가 다르다.
258|
259|숱한 싸움과 생사의 갈림길에서 다듬어진 살기는 원초적인 두려움을 불러일으킨다.
260|
261|어지간히 담 큰 사람도 오줌을 지릴 정도인데, 이러한 것에 더욱 민감한 개는 말할 것도 없었다.
262|
263|끼이잉. 낑낑.
264|
265|살기를 느낀 도사견들이 이빨을 감추고, 꼬리를 배 아래로 감춘 채 납작 엎드렸다. 불안하게 흔들리는 눈동자는 감히 내 쪽을 쳐다보지도 못하고 있다.
266|
267|“옳지. 착하다.”
268|
269|서걱.
270|
271|손에 맺힌 수강(手罡)으로 철창을 가르며 정원으로 발을 디딘 그 순간.
272|
273|부드러운 점막을 통과한 듯한 기분과 함께 요란한 사이렌 소리가 울려 퍼졌다.
274|
275|위이이이이잉!
276|
277|띠링.
278|
279|
280|
281|- [알람 마법]이 발동했습니다!
282|
283|- [소리 차단 마법]이 발동했습니다! 모든 소음이 저택 밖으로 새어 나가지 않습니다!
284|
285|- [시야 차단 마법]이 발동했습니다! 내부의 광경이 밖에서 보이지 않습니다!
286|
287|
288|
289|나름 방비를 해 둔 모양이군. 오히려 잘됐다.
290|
291|마법이 작동됨과 동시에 저택 안의 불이 환하게 밝혀졌다.
292|
293|그 안에서 다급하게 움직이는 수십의 인기척이 느껴지더니 곧 철제 현관문이 폭발하듯 터져 나갔다.
294|
295|쾅!
296|
297|가장 먼저 모습을 드러낸 다섯 명의 사내. 그 중심에 ‘꼬리’가 있었다.
298|
299|평범해 보이던 중년인의 눈빛은 살인자의 그것처럼 변해 있었다.
300|
301|
302|
303|[Lv.95 임영준]
304|
305|
306|
307|“넌…….”
308|
309|일그러진 얼굴. 흔들리는 눈동자. 내 얼굴을 알아본 것이 틀림없다.
310|
311|나는 놈을 향해 활짝 웃어 주었다.
312|
313|“마을 청년회에서 나왔습니다.”
314|
315|“진태경!”
316|
317|“아닌데요. 뚱인데요.”
318|
319|“여기는 어떻게 알고 왔지?”
320|

[P84]

[P85]

[P86]
That would make things easier.

[P87]
“Approaching carelessly could backfire. So for today, we should stop here and—”

“Pardon?”

[P95]
“Hunter Jin Taekyung. Nothing is more dangerous than an enemy whose capabilities you haven’t assessed.”

[P96]
“Yes. I know.”

[P97]
“I understand that your skills are exceptional, but…”

[P98]

[P99]
“There could be dozens of A-rank Hunters like the man I observed waiting for you.”

[P100]
“It’s fine. Honestly, the Three Idiots looked stronger than that guy.”

[P101]
“…?”

[P102]
“Don’t worry about it. He just reminded me of some people I know.”

[P103]

[P104]
“No. I’m always thinking about you.”

[P105]
“Eek.”

[P106]
“Be quiet before I punish you with a confession.”

[P107]
“Aah!”

[P108]
*Whew. I’m fucking cool. No wonder women run screaming.*

[P109]

[P110]
“I want to stop you, but I can’t.”

[P111]
His expression was impossible to describe.

[P112]
“Every crazy thing you’ve done has always succeeded.”

[P113]
“You’ve got me figured out. Then move exactly as I said. It’ll all be over within an hour at most.”

[P114]
“Black Hunters… Those men have been trained to hunt humans, not monsters. Be careful.”

[P115]
I couldn’t hold back a laugh.

[P116]
“Good. That happens to be my specialty, too.”

[P117]
“Pardon?”

[P118]

[P119]

[P120]

[P121]
I had become Jin Taekyung, a man of Murim.

[P123]
Grrrrr.

[P124]

[P125]

[P126]
“If I hear you bark, you’re becoming dog-meat soup.”

[P127]
Unless the dogs had attended a Korean language academy, there was no way they could understand me.

[P128]
But killing intent was another matter.

[P129]
Killing intent, honed through countless battles and brushes with death, awakened a primal fear.

[P130]
It was enough to make even the stouthearted piss themselves. Dogs, which were even more sensitive to such things, stood no chance.

[P131]
Whine. Whimper.

[P132]

[P133]
“That’s right. Good dogs.”

[P134]
Slice.

[P135]

[P137]
Wheeeeeeeeng!

[P138]
Ding.

>
> **Sound-Blocking Magic** has activated! No noise will escape the mansion!
>
> **Vision-Blocking Magic** has activated! The scene inside cannot be seen from outside!

They had taken some precautions.

[P141]
Even better.

[P142]

[P143]

[P144]
Bang!

[P145]

[P146]

[P147]
> **System**
>
> **Lv. 95 Im Yeongjun**

[P148]
“You…”

[P150]
I gave him a broad smile.

[P151]
“I’m with the village youth association.”

[P152]
“Jin Taekyung!”

[P153]
“Nope. This is Patrick.”

[P154]
“How did you find this place?”

[P155]

[P156]

[P157]
“Don’t tell me you came alone.”

[P158]

[P159]
“Looks like you did.”

[P160]
His mouth twisted.

[P161]
“Fucking idiot. There’s a limit to how ignorant you can be of the way the world works.”

[P162]
“That’s what I wanted to say to you. You should’ve chosen your target more carefully.”

[P163]
“That D-rank nobody who barely qualifies as a Hunter? Did they reattach his arm?”

[P164]
“They did, but… apparently, there’ll be some lasting damage. So I came to collect a little compensation.”

[P165]
“I meant to kill him, but I held back. Be grateful it ended there. If you don’t want something worse to happen, lie low and keep quiet.”

[P166]
“Something worse already happened, and lying low isn’t in my nature. I’m not particularly grateful, either. Isn’t that why I came here?”

[P167]
Im Yeongjun gave a short laugh.

[P168]
“Kid, I know you’re excited because everyone around you treats you like a big shot, but don’t make the mistake of thinking we’re ordinary Hunters.”

[P169]

[P170]
I swept my gaze over the mansion.

[P171]

[P172]
“One, five, ten… Twenty-eight in all. You’ve gathered quite a crowd.”

[P173]
“…”

[P174]
“How?”

[P175]
“I’m not an ordinary Hunter, either.”

[P176]

“Three. Hand over the three who took part in the attack two days ago, including you. The rest disarm and tell me everything you know. Do that, and I’ll spare your lives.”

[P178]
“You crazy bastard.”

[P179]
“Good. I was worried you might accept.”

That was my first and last offer.

[P181]
There wouldn’t be another.

[P182]
*Open Inventory. Equip White Flame.*

[P183]
The moment the cool spear shaft filled my hand, Im Yeongjun screamed.

[P184]
“Kill him!”

[P185]
That was the signal.

[P186]
Dozens of Black Hunters who had been waiting in breathless silence smashed through the walls and windows and surged toward me.

[P187]
Crash! Shhhhk!

[P188]
A rain of countless blades and arrowheads poured in from every direction.

[P189]
As I watched them come, my eyes turned cold.

[P190]
“You picked the wrong person to mess with.”

[P191]
Fwoooosh!

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 276

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃276화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|중년인은 어디에서나 볼 수 있는 흔한 동네 아저씨였다.
  6|
  7|귀밑부터 턱까지 이어진 푸르스름한 수염 자국. 실용성을 강조한 등산복은 뱃살로 불룩하다.
  8|
  9|이른 새벽, 졸음이 뚝뚝 떨어지는 눈으로 스트레칭을 끝낸 그는 논두렁 길을 천천히 뛰기 시작했다.
 10|
 11|헛둘헛둘, 아저씨 특유의 구성진 소리까지 곁들여 가면서.
 12|
 13|김 집사가 찾았다는 ‘꼬리’가 바로 그였다.
 14|
 15|“이 아저씨 맞아요?”
 16|
 17|어디서나 볼 수 있는 승합차 내부, 김 집사가 마법으로 녹화한 영상을 보던 송송이가 미심쩍다는 표정으로 중얼거렸다.
 18|
 19|“평범해 보이는데.”
 20|
 21|“비범해 보이는 게 더 이상하지 않을까. 블랙 헌터가 9급 공무원 같은 느낌은 아니잖아.”
 22|
 23|“아무리 그래도 저 아저씨는 너무 평범해 보여서. 전투 헌터들만 알아볼 수 있는 뭐 그런 게 있나?”
 24|
 25|“있지.”
 26|
 27|나는 조깅을 끝마치고 저택으로 들어가는 중년인의 모습을 뚫어질 듯이 응시했다.
 28|
 29|지금 보는 것은 단순한 영상에 불과하니 공력은 느낄 수 없다. 그러나 아무리 천재적인 연기자라 해도 미세한 움직임 하나에서 자신을 드러내기 마련이다.
 30|
 31|그리고 내게는 연기를 꿰뚫어 볼 수 있는 안목이 있었다.
 32|
 33|“절정 고수…….”
 34|
 35|“응?”
 36|
 37|내 혼잣말에 반응한 사람은 송송이뿐만이 아니었다.
 38|
 39|그게 무슨 소리냐는 듯한 최 팀장과 김 집사의 시선에 말을 이었다.
 40|
 41|“……가 아니라, A급 헌터네요.”
 42|
 43|“뭐라 말씀하셨던 것 같은데. 절정 고수라고 하셨나.”
 44|
 45|“놉. 잘못 들으신 듯.”
 46|
 47|이럴 땐 철벽이 답이다. 당사자가 안 했다는데 어쩔 거야.
 48|
 49|석연찮은 눈빛도 잠시, 최 팀장과 김 집사도 내 의견에 동조하듯 고개를 끄덕였다.
 50|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
